source_text:
ἀλλ' οὔτε κατ' οἶκον κοινόν· οὐκ ἔξεστι γὰρ Χριστιανῷ

δι' ὀφθαλμῶν μετεωρίζεσθαι καὶ ῥεμβασμῶν τοῦ νοός, ἀλλ' ἐγγεγραμμένα καὶ
ἐντετυπωμένα ἔστω πᾶσι τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν. 34 εἴ τις τὸν θεῖον τοῦ θεοῦ λόγου
χαρακτῆρα κατὰ τὴν σάρκωσιν ἐξ ὑλικῶν χρωμάτων ἐπιτηδεύει κατανοῆσαι... ἔστω
ἀνάθεμα.
thought_title: No images even in a common house; anathema on depicting the incarnate Word
orientation: Epiphanius is closing his testament to the citizens, extending the prohibition on images from churches and cemeteries to any common house and pronouncing anathema on those who try to grasp the incarnate Word through material colors.
pass_a_gloss: But not even in a common house; for it is not lawful for a Christian to be distracted through the eyes and the wanderings of the mind, but let the things toward God be written and impressed in all. If anyone deliberately endeavors to comprehend the divine character of God's Word according to the incarnation from material colors, let him be anathema.

choices.why: The adjective κοινόν modifies οἶκον, indicating an ordinary or private dwelling as opposed to churches and cemeteries already mentioned.
The verb means to be lifted up or carried away; in this context it describes the mind being drawn away through the eyes, so 'distracted' captures the sense.
ῥεμβασμός denotes roaming or wandering; with τοῦ νοός it describes mental wandering away from God.
The two perfect passive participles describe how the things toward God should be fixed in all people; 'written and impressed' preserves the metaphor of inscription and stamping.
ἐπιτηδεύει means to practice or make a deliberate effort; with the infinitive κατανοῆσαι it conveys an intentional attempt to grasp mentally.
rejected: makes it his business to perceive

choices.why: The imperative ἔστω with ἀνάθεμα is a formal curse formula; the glossary requires 'anathema' rather than 'accursed' or 'condemned'.

pass_b_english: But not even in an ordinary house. A Christian must not be distracted through the eyes and the wanderings of the mind; rather, the things that pertain to God should be written and impressed upon everyone. If anyone deliberately endeavors to comprehend the divine character of God's Word according to the incarnation from material colors, let him be anathema.

last_rejected.quote: A Christian must not be distracted through the eyes and the wanderings of the mind
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ ἔξεστι γὰρ Χριστιανῷ δι' ὀφθαλμῶν μετεωρίζεσθαι καὶ ῥεμβασμῶν τοῦ νοός
last_rejected.why: Source says 'it is not lawful for a Christian' (impersonal), English makes it a command/must.
last_rejected.fix: For it is not lawful for a Christian to be distracted through the eyes and wanderings of the mind.
last_rejected.ruling: οὐκ ἔξεστι means 'not lawful/permitted'; 'must not' conveys same prohibition adequately.

last_rejected.quote: the things that pertain to God should be written and impressed upon everyone
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐγγεγραμμένα καὶ ἐντετυπωμένα ἔστω πᾶσι τὰ πρὸς τὸν θεόν
last_rejected.why: Source is passive 'let them be written,' English 'should be written' weakens the command force.
last_rejected.fix: Let the things that pertain to God be inscribed and impressed upon all.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔστω is third-person imperative 'let be'; 'should be' is acceptable English rendering of directive force.

last_rejected.quote: If anyone deliberately endeavors to comprehend the divine character of God's Word according to the incarnation from material colors, let him be anathema
last_rejected.source_quote: εἴ τις τὸν θεῖον τοῦ θεοῦ λόγου χαρακτῆρα κατὰ τὴν σάρκωσιν ἐξ ὑλικῶν χρωμάτων ἐπιτηδεύει κατανοῆσαι... ἔστω ἀνάθεμα
last_rejected.why: Ellipsis in source (ἔστω ἀνάθεμα separated by gap) not marked; translator may have missed something.
last_rejected.fix: If anyone deliberately endeavors to comprehend the divine character of God's Word according to the incarnation from material colors... let him be anathema.
last_rejected.ruling: Source ellipsis (...) is minor; ἔστω ἀνάθεμα present and translated; no meaning lost.
